NOTICE AND CALL OF A SPECIAL MEETING
OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF AZUSA
TO THE MEMBERS OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF AZUSA:
NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that a Special Meeting of the City Council of the City of Azusa is hereby called to be held Monday, February 25, 2019 at 06:30 p.m. at Azusa Light and Water Conference Room.
Said Special Meeting shall be for discussing, hearing and taking action on the items listed below:
AGENDA
A.
PRELIMINARY BUSINESS
1.
Call to Order
2.
Roll Call
3.
Flag Salute
B.
PUBLIC COMMENT Please note that public comments are welcomed by recognition of the
Mayor, and are limited to items listed on this special meeting agenda.
A Person/Group shall be allowed to speak without interruption for up to three (3) minutes maximum time, only on items appearing on this agenda, and only if a vote is taken, in accordance with the Special Meeting Provisions of the Brown Act. Public Comment will be limited to thirty (30) minutes time
C.
FISCAL YEAR 2018-19 GENERAL FUND MID-YEAR BUDGET REVIEW AND ADJUSTMENTS.
RECOMMENDED ACTION: 1) Receive, review and file Fiscal Year 2018-19 second quarter budget-to-actual report ending December 31, 2018; and
2) Adopt Resolution No. 2019-C06 approving the listed proposed budget amendments; and
3) Direct Staff to report back to Council at a future study session regarding a fiscal sustainability assessment and near and long-term budget impacts for direction and next steps.
C- Staff Report - Mid-Year Budget Review FY 2018-19
D.

minutes_text:
CITY OF AZUSA
  MINUTES OF THE SPECIAL MEETING OF
  THE CITY COUNCIL
  MONDAY, FEBRUARY 25, 2019 – 6:30 P.M.

The City Council of the City of Azusa, met in Special Session at the above date and time in the Azusa Light & Water
Conference Room, located at 729 N. Azusa Avenue, Azusa, CA 91702.

Mayor Rocha called the meeting to order at 6:52 P.M.

ROLL CALL: Roll call was taken by City Clerk Cornejo.

PRESENT: COUNCILMEMBERS: GONZALES, CARRILLO, MACIAS, ALVAREZ, ROCHA
ABSENT: COUNCILMEMBERS: NONE

ALSO PRESENT

Elected Officials: City Clerk Cornejo.
Staff Members: City Manager Gonzalez, City Attorney Ferre, Director of Finance Johnson, Director of Human
Resources and Risk Management Bragg, Director of Public Works/City Engineer Bobadilla, Director of Economic &
Community Development Marquez, Utilities Director Robledo, Chief of Police Hunt, Director of Information Technology
and Library Services Graf, Director of Recreation and Family Services Carpenter, Chief Deputy City Clerk Garcia.

PUBLIC COMMENT

Mr. Jorge V. Rosales commended Staff for the concise and transparent Mid-Year Budget Review Staff Report.

FISCAL YEAR 2018-19 GENERAL FUND MID-YEAR BUDGET REVIEW AND ADJUSTMENTS

Director of Finance Johnson presented the 2018-19 mid-year budget review stating that guiding budget principles are to
match costs with revenues, maintain reserve policy, address unfunded liabilities, maintain essential services to the
community, and avoid using one-time monies for long term costs; total revenues are at 31% of adjusted budget; and
expenditures are at 48% of budget. A mid-year revenue increase of $205,195 and decrease of $566,500 were proposed;
and with the proposed budget adjustments, an estimated additional $800,000 will be added to the Overall Fund Balance.
An amended financial forecast was presented, which included increasing pension costs, one time property sales, and
salary savings resulting in a FY 2018-19 projected surplus of $2.8 million; however, the surplus is due to the $2.7 million
sale of Block 36 and $1 million in salary savings; excluding the one-time monies, the City has an ongoing budget deficit
of approximately $800k. The projected year-end cash balance for FY 2018-19 is $12.7 million with a reserves target of
approximately $10 million. Potential significant budget impacts include labor contract negotiations, rising pension costs,
unfunded pension and OPEB liabilities, replenishing reserves, and infrastructure and facility needs; Staff is currently
undergoing a fiscal sustainability assessment to review existing contracts and franchise agreements to ensure the City is
capturing all contractual obligations, examine areas of organizational efficiency opportunities, and explore extraordinary
measures to generate additional revenues.

In response to questions posed by the Council, Staff clarified that Block 37 sale proceeds were included in the FY 2019-
20 forecast as a best case scenario, should the property sell; the FY 2019-20 budget is still being developed; the City will
be experiencing a structural deficit over the next five years, and will need to decrease expenses and increase revenues; the
goal of the fiscal sustainability assessment is to help realize new revenues and efficiencies to cut costs.

Discussion ensued regarding the need to increase revenues, the projected structural deficit, local sales tax measures across
the region, and competing tax measures.

Councilmember Carrillo offered Resolution No. 2019-C06

A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF AZUSA APPROVING AND ADOPTING THE MID-
YEAR BUDGET ADJUSTMENTS FOR THE CITY OF AZUSA
 Moved by Councilmember Carrillo, seconded by Councilmember Gonzales, and carried by unanimous vote of the Council
to receive, review and file Fiscal Year 2018-19 second quarter budget-to-actual report ending December 31, 2108; adopt
Resolution 2019-C06 approving and adopting the proposed mid-year budget amendments; and direct Staff to report back
to Council at a future study session regarding a fiscal sustainability assessment and near and long-term budget impacts for
direction and next steps.

AYES:  COUNCILMEMBERS: GONZALES, CARRILLO, MACIAS, ALVAREZ, ROCHA
NOES:  COUNCILMEMBERS: NONE
ABSENT:  COUNCILMEMBERS: NONE

ADJOURNMENT

The meeting was adjourned by consensus of the City Council.

TIME OF ADJOURNMENT: 7:21 P.M.
